contradiction_examples.a_text: Unprocessed red meat consumption is not associated with incident stroke.
contradiction_examples.b_text: Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with an 11% increased risk of stroke.
contradiction_examples.explanation: Claim A asserts that unprocessed red meat consumption has no association with incident stroke, whereas Claim B states that it is associated with an increased risk of stroke.

contradiction_examples.a_text: The decreased risk of myocardial infarction was similar between men consuming less than 10 g of alcohol per drinking day and those consuming 30 g or more.
contradiction_examples.b_text: Increased alcohol consumption is log-linearly associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.94 per 100 g/week higher consumption).
contradiction_examples.explanation: Claim A indicates that the risk reduction for myocardial infarction is similar regardless of alcohol intake level, whereas Claim B asserts a continuous, log-linear decrease in risk with higher alcohol consumption.

contradiction_examples.a_text: Alcohol consumption is not significantly associated with overall incident stroke compared with non-drinking (pooled adjusted RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06).
contradiction_examples.b_text: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR 1.14 per 100 g/week higher consumption).
contradiction_examples.explanation: Claim A finds no significant overall association between alcohol consumption and incident stroke, whereas Claim B reports that higher alcohol consumption is linearly associated with an increased stroke risk.

contradiction_examples.a_text: Alcohol consumption exhibits a curvilinear J-shaped dose-response relationship with the relative risk of ischemic stroke.
contradiction_examples.b_text: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR 1.14 per 100 g/week higher consumption).
contradiction_examples.explanation: Claim A asserts a J-shaped curvilinear dose-response relationship between alcohol consumption and stroke risk, whereas Claim B asserts a linear relationship where higher consumption is consistently associated with higher risk.

contradiction_examples.a_text: Unprocessed red meat intake is not associated with incident diabetes mellitus.
contradiction_examples.b_text: Higher intake of red meat is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
contradiction_examples.explanation: Claim A finds no association between unprocessed red meat intake and incident diabetes, whereas Claim B reports that higher intake of red meat is associated with an increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
